leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members prefer a single-part prize on topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, and all six now name the same trio, Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. All pair the Z2 theory with the HgTe quantum-well observation, though citation wording differs ('theoretical discovery' versus 'prediction', 'first experimental realisation' versus 'experimental discovery'). Danielsson, Olsson and Pearce each opened with Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan and moved to include Mele after reading the ballots, and Eriksson moved his first choice from B017 to B006. What is not shared is how much weight to give the 2016 topological-phases prize; all six record the omission of Hasan and of the HgTe proposers (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) as the main cost of the configuration. Because several moves followed colleagues' arguments, the agreement within this group is partly convergent and not fully independent.

Two members, both atomic physicists, prefer a single-part prize on optical lattice clocks with Katori and Ye. They argue for a distinct invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms), demonstrated 10^-18 performance, reach into constants tests and geodesy, and the cleanest attribution on the shortlist. Both list B006 as their first alternative and both discount their own field proximity. They differ in emphasis: Kroll would not wait for the redefinition of the second, while Lindroth keeps B006 as an alternative chiefly because attribution there is unresolved. Neither rejects B006 on scientific grounds.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members propose single-part prizes: six prefer B006, two prefer B047, and each of those two names B006 as first alternative.
Within each camp the laureates are identical: Kane, Mele and Molenkamp for B006 (all six supporters) and Katori and Ye for B047 (both supporters).
Members who discuss the maturity of B006 regard it as mature, with about two decades of independent confirmation by transport, ARPES and STM.
Members describe B047 as having the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and several describe B006 as having the broader consequence across subfields.

Members who comment on B038 (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) regard it as a strong, mature candidate that is hard to place immediately after the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize, and note Girvin's omission from the credited names.
Members who comment on B017 (Eriksson, Danielsson, Mehlig, Pearce, Kroll, Lindroth) treat it as a strong candidate whose open question is maturity, not concept.
scientific_disputes: Whether the Z2 insulator and quantum spin Hall effect are a distinct discovery from the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions and phases of matter. Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce argue they are distinct (time-reversal symmetry and spin-orbit coupling versus 1D chains and quantum Hall topology); Johansson says the increment must be argued, and Eriksson and Pearce report that Lindroth worries about reduced appetite for a second topological prize.

Whether optical lattice clocks are a new invention or a refinement of the precision-spectroscopy toolbox recognised in 2005 (frequency comb) and 2012 (trapped-ion control). Kroll and Lindroth say magic-wavelength trapping is a distinct principle; Danielsson, Eriksson, Olsson and Pearce either say this is the crux or say they cannot judge it as non-specialists.

Whether circuit QED is a new phenomenon or mainly an enabling architecture for quantum technology (Danielsson, Johansson, Olsson, Pearce), and whether it is distinct enough from the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.

Whether ultracold-atom quantum simulation (B034) and trapped-ion computation (B031) have yet delivered their decisive scientific payoff (Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig), and whether their overlap through Zoller and Cirac argues for combining them or for delaying both.
attribution_disputes: B006 trio: Danielsson, Olsson and Pearce initially proposed Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan (theory plus two experiments); Eriksson, Johansson and Mehlig proposed Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. All six now propose the latter. Danielsson and Johansson say they could accept the Hasan version if colleagues find Mele's omission less costly.

Omitted B006 contributors: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal; Zhang is deceased), Hasan and the first 3D ARPES observations, and the 3D theory of Fu, Moore, Balents and Roy. Mehlig argues Hasan's claim is partly carried by Kane and Mele through the Fu-Kane-Mele 3D theory; Danielsson and Olsson describe the 3D priority question (Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3) as contested.
B047: Kroll and Lindroth ask whether ion-clock groups or other early lattice-clock contributors should be credited beyond Katori and Ye; neither says the supplied names are wrong.
B038: Girvin's omission despite his co-authorship of the 2004 theory proposal is raised by Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce; Kroll also raises the Devoret lineage.
B048: Olsson raises that a two-name credit for IceCube compresses a collaboration of hundreds plus AMANDA and Baikal predecessors; Johansson asks the same about AMANDA.
maturity_disputes: B017 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene): Eriksson now treats the unresolved pairing mechanism as a reason B017 can wait, while still calling it reproduced by many groups; Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce call it early. Kroll adds that Cao and Dean are absent from the credited names.
B047: whether the pending redefinition of the second should delay the prize. Lindroth raised it; Kroll, Olsson and Pearce say no; Eriksson asks Kroll whether it should.

B048 (IceCube): Olsson regards the source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) as statistically modest and prefers a later year; Pearce ranked it second in his opening ballot but does not propose it.
B006: Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson say maturity is not a concern; the open question for this ballot is the room left after 2016, not its maturity.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (B038): directs WACQT at Chalmers, works in superconducting circuits, has ties to Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson, and notes that Chalmers hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize; he says he discounted his own B038 enthusiasm and now prefers B006. Mehlig asks whether that connection should be weighed when counting first-place support for B038.
Olsson: shares an institution (Chalmers) with Johansson, who ranked B038 first in the opening ballot; she documents no connection to any credited name.

Kroll: doctoral research stay in John Hall's laboratory, a lineage adjacent to Jun Ye's work (B047); he also flags WACQT, Lund quantum-information and quantum-memory ties relevant to B031 and B038 if either is discussed. No direct collaboration with Katori or Ye is documented.

Lindroth: field proximity to atomic precision spectroscopy (B047, B031, B034); no credited name appears among her documented collaborators, and she notes that her shared atomic-physics background with Kroll should not substitute for argument.
Eriksson: possible bias toward band-structure and DFT topics (B026 and the materials side of B006 and B017); no personal link to credited persons.
Pearce (chair): astroparticle background is closest to B048 (IceCube); no IceCube collaboration is documented in his profile. He ranked B048 second in the opening ballot and does not propose it.
Danielsson and Mehlig report no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: B006 versus B047 as the single prize: once the 2016 overlap, the omission of Hasan and the HgTe proposers, and the 2005 and 2012 metrology overlap are weighed in the same terms, does either camp change its preferred ballot?

For B006, does any member hold that Hasan should replace Mele (or Molenkamp) in the trio? If Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is kept, what citation wording avoids implying that the 3D materials discovery is being recognised?

Can members state in one sentence why the Z2 insulator and quantum spin Hall effect are a different discovery from the topological phases honoured in 2016, so that Johansson and Lindroth can say whether the overlap concern is resolved?

Can the atomic-physics members state why magic-wavelength lattice trapping is a separate invention from frequency combs (2005) and trapped-ion control (2012), and say whether ion-clock groups should change the B047 credit?

Is a second prize in the superconducting-circuit community in consecutive years acceptable for B038? If any member thinks it could be, what is the precise distinction from the 2025 prize, and how should Girvin's omission be handled?

Would any member support B017 for 2026, or a two-part prize pairing B006 with B047 (noting Johansson's point that the union of names would exceed three unless B006 shrinks)? If not, what evidence on pairing mechanism or timing would change positions?
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 files show a majority position (six of eight: B006 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp) and a firmly held minority position (two of eight: B047 with Katori and Ye), each camp naming the other's ballot as its first alternative. Disagreement within the majority has largely been resolved on the trio; the remaining issues are the attribution cost of omitting Hasan and the HgTe proposers and the 2016 overlap. The minority case rests on attribution cleanliness and a distinctness argument that non-atomic members say they cannot fully test. Several positions moved on colleagues' arguments, so the counts should not be read as independent assessments. These counts describe stated preferences only and are not a ruling.
